key_insight: The paper proposes generalized second-order routing for Multi-State Linear Attention, aiming to route queries using richer information than average query–key alignment alone.
problem_solved: Standard self-attention has quadratic time complexity, limiting long-context scaling. Existing Multi-State Linear Attention compresses context into separate memories but routes between them using only mean alignment, potentially overlooking useful matching information.
method: Split the input sequence into segments and compress each segment into its own memory state.
Introduce generalized second-order routing to move beyond mean-only query–segment alignment.
Aggregate information from the segment memories; detailed routing equations are unavailable in the truncated abstract.
impact: The approach targets more effective memory selection for efficient long-context models. Its practical speed, memory, and quality gains cannot be verified from the supplied excerpt.
visual_elements: Sequence-to-memory diagram: token segments compressed into separate memory blocks.
Routing comparison: mean-only alignment versus richer second-order alignment.

Conceptual scaling chart contrasting quadratic self-attention with linear attention, without implying measured results.
paper_title: Multi-State Linear Attention with Generalized Second-Order Routing
paper_authors: Hee Seung Hwang, Sanghyuk Chun, Xindi Wu, Olga Russakovsky, Zhiwei Deng
